rv.q: Andrew Gallant's staging sets the audience on either side of the home where four generations of one family face the aftereffects of abandonment, as well as the lingering pull of nostalgia. An apple tree provides symbolic sustenance (as in "the apple doesn't fall far from.
Admirably performed and encased in a central story that many will be able to recognize and connect with, Smokefall holds valuable insights.
Wild Door Theatre’s debut production does much to dazzle audiences and elevate the drama from a merely well-trodden path to a journey of familial restitution and restoration.
If you’re in the mood for an even-kelled and thoughtful production that explores themes of repeating mistakes and families, Smokefall would be a good fit for you.

I will tell you that while I was impressed with this company taking on this unusual play combining realism with a little bit of vaudeville, as well as a family drama that moves about in generations, which might be confusing for many.

cn.t: Critics praise Wild Door Theater's ambitious Chicago debut with Noah Haidle's philosophical family drama, commending its deeper exploration of family dynamics across generations and its bold storytelling approach.
